english_verification.review_scope: Read the B20 opening history, the B20-to-B54 formation and Necroeconomics initialisation branch, representative B54 mission script lines, and the fixed-revision Esthíl Wiki chunk. The Wiki chunk is only a short country frame; no full history or exhaustive mission/event audit was performed. National-idea assembly is outside this receipt. The primary compared native idea names/descriptions with current English localisation keys (formatting codes stripped); B32 upgraded Farranean originals also use their separate flavour file. Wide source bounds are locator envelopes, not exhaustive line-by-line audits. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The dedicated Esthíl Wiki chunk is a short country frame and does not establish detailed history; subsequent historical claims remain bounded to the existing cited research and current local text.
The 2026-07-09 mission-file modification date is not a verified first-release date.
No full reachability audit or in-game playtest of the War of the Black Tower was performed.

rationale.campaign_length: 31 direct B54 missions plus the B20 adventurer prologue make this a campaign that runs into the mid-to-late game.
rationale.colonization: The opening involves adventurer migration and settlement in Escann; after formation, expansion relies mainly on land conquest.
rationale.complexity: The adventurer opening, a dedicated resource interface, magical research, core development, and the endgame war all demand planning.
rationale.dark_story: Corpse industries, taxation of souls, purges, lich rule, and a continent-wide war of terror define the campaign.
rationale.difficulty: The country snowballs strongly in ordinary wars, but the War of the Black Tower tests that preparation through simultaneous internal and external crises.
rationale.diplomacy: The route deliberately creates diplomatic isolation; by the end, the main pressure comes from a coalition against Esthíl.
rationale.early_pressure: The Order of the Iron Sceptre has a powerful mage, but must still settle and expand quickly in chaotic Escann.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The dedicated necromantic project, mage state, lich, and Morgurax are core gameplay, not side features.
rationale.narrative_density: The story moves in a concentrated sequence from forbidden research to a necroeconomy, the War of the Black Tower, and a Dark Empire.
rationale.tall_play: The necroeconomy strengthens farmland, mines, industry, and the Castonath core, rewarding concentrated development.
rationale.trade_economy: Undead labour, food, gold, mining, and industry supply one another and underpin the war machine.
rationale.warfare: Adventurer competition, conquest in Escann, and the War of the Black Tower make military strength central throughout.

identity.appearance: Start as the Order of the Iron Sceptre (B20) in 1444; complete Escanni adventurer settlement and form B54 to switch to its dedicated mission tree.

predecessors.relationship: The sole dedicated narrative predecessor; forming B54 changes the Tag and switches the mission tree.

successors.relationship: An optional formable successor; forming it replaces the mission tree, and it is treated as a separate campaign entry.

gaps.reason: No unambiguous tag/culture national idea definition found; no predecessor inference.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: With the outbreak of the Greentide, vast swathes of land across Escann have been ruined. Were it not for the selfless acts of the brave magisters, in defiance of the Magisterium, the Greentide would have surely overcome all of Cannor. Esthíl itself has been established by these outlawed magisters, and it is with open arms that we accept any and all magic users who wish to join our realm.

description.text: Throughout the lands of Cannor, magic is seen as a force that acts behind closed doors, in secret. That is not so for Esthíl. This is an Arcane Dawn for the world, when all may practice magic freely without fear of repercussion.

description.text: The Esthíli Academy of Magic is the foremost magical education institution in all of Escann. While there are those elsewhere who pretend to compete with our title, such as the Núrcestirans, all know that only the most elite of candidates are accepted and graduate from Esthíl.

description.text: The Magisterium foolishly all but banned necromancy, one of the most powerful schools of magic. It is only fitting that we should sanction its usage as the other schools of magic are treated, for a loyal necromancer can bring many boons to our nation. Besides free manual labor, the necromancer themselves would remain loyal to the one cause that permits them.

description.text: A horrid manuscript found in a long-forgotten vault, the Grimoire of Tenebral Secrets lives up to its name. It bestows great power to those who can read and understand it, but at the risk of immediate death if not worthy.

description.text: Far below the shadowy and ominous Castle Esthíl, the Mystic Vaults are a vast labyrinth filled with countless magical artifacts and spellbooks. From far and wide magical artifacts are tithed to fill the ever-expanding needs of the elite magisters.

description.text: In the cosmology of the Black Doctrine, all beings with the capability to use magic are positioned somewhere in a great chain of ascension, sometimes called the 'Ascendant Path'. At the near end of this path are the so-called 'potentiates', people who have latent magical ability but lack the discipline to use it in any consistent and meaningful way. At the far end lies the Universal Mind, the great dispassionate, impersonal intellect which suffuses all the world. The Ascendant is the being who traverses this great path, growing in each stage until they achieve a true union with that purest Intellect. Officially, every Sorcerer-King was Ascendant, though any serious discussion with heretics will reveal that this is a point of much contention.

description.text: The Week of Ascension was simultaneously one of the world's most egalitarian institutions and one of its most stratified. Regardless of social class, all non-magical subjects participated in the same festivals and shared in the same activities during the seven-day celebration of virtue. However, every magic user was kept separate from these festivities, instead joining the Sorcerer-King in the Charred Tower for a week of celebration, debauchery, and furious politicking.

description.text: There have been various attempts to regulate and control magical research throughout the history of the mortal realms. Indeed, perhaps one of the truest signs of a healthy state has been its ability to impose at least some basic restrictions on the activities of mages. In the Black Demesne, to suggest such regulations was not merely seen as foolish, but rather a blasphemous heresy against Doctrine itself. Any law which restricted the development of Intellect was opposed to Doctrine, and restrictions on magic were the most heinous of these.

description.text: Though the non-magical classes could not ascend to the highest rungs of state power in the Demesne, and though they had very limited rights, they nonetheless rose in prominence. Precisely because the most powerful positions were restricted to magic users, these same powerful people often chose to surround themselves with those who could not possibly be a threat. They often promoted members of the non-magical class based on pure competence, justifying the high placement on the basis of intellectual virtue. This was in stark contrast to many other kingdoms, where promotion was by right of blood alone.

description.text: Undead are useful on the field of battle as brute soldiers, but they have very limited capacity to think for themselves or listen to verbal orders. Thus, the Demesne had great need for living scouts, battlefield engineers, and officers. Such positions were an excellent way for non-magical subjects to climb the social ladder by making themselves valuable to mages. Every time war was declared, a great influx of some of the Demesne's most intelligent, driven, and ambitious people came to serve the army in all manner of roles, a pattern that would later earn the moniker of 'the Reaper's Gift'.

description.text: In most societies, mages are typically reclusive academics who have little interest in battlefield glory, and only a smaller portion have the inclination to take up arms and lend their talents to the field of glory. In the Demesne, it was an expectation and personal obligation for every magical initiate to serve for at least some time in the military. This vastly greater pool of magical manpower allowed the Demesne to turn the entire upper officer corps into the exclusive province of mages, allowing decentralized and responsive magical tactics that were far more impressive than any single sorcerer could achieve alone.

description.text: At its greatest extent, the Black Demesne had eight Acolytes, each of whom wore an ebony ring, numbered from the First to the Eighth in order of magical prowess and prominence within the court. The Sorcerer-King wore a matching ring of dark gold, signifying dominance, which would become known as the Ninth ring. Theoretically, as long as one wore the ring of an Acolyte, one was honorbound to give nothing but absolute loyalty to the legitimate bearer of the Ninth ring in all matters. This reminder of hierarchy and control fortified the political order of the Demesne's upper class.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid this if you dislike institutionalised atrocities, complex mechanics, diplomatic isolation, or preparing for a sudden large-scale endgame war.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Use the Order's powerful mage to win the early Escanni adventurer contest; form B54 in midgame, expand for resources and build the necroeconomy, then use industry, magic, and undead armies to survive the War of the Black Tower.
player_overview.overview: Begin as the mage-led adventurer company, the Order of the Iron Sceptre, and form Esthíl after settling. Varina first pursues the ideal of making the dead bear burdens that would otherwise fall on the living, then brings corpses, souls, and undead armies into a state rationing system. Midgame revolves around the Necroeconomics project, Harvest Fields, and Dead Mines; late game brings the flying fortress Morgurax and the War of the Black Tower, pitting you against internal rebellion and an external coalition. Magic, development, and aggressive warfare are tightly bound together in this dark, lengthy campaign.
player_overview.recommended_for: For players who enjoy dark national narratives, magical projects, resource allocation, core development, and large-scale conquest reinforcing one another.
signature_features: A tier-three Necroeconomics project and dedicated resource interface let you allocate the dead among labour, soldiers, construction, and development.
Varina, the path to lichdom, the mage coven, and the Death Tax carry the story from an academic ideal to a totalitarian system.
The flying fortress Morgurax and the War of the Black Tower create a high-pressure finale that rewards preparation of finances, forts, and strategic depth.
player_overview.tagline: Turn necromancy into a national economy, rebuild Escann with undead labour, and pilot a flying Black Tower against the continent.

reasons: Necroeconomics is an operable second-population economy, not just numerical flavour.
The national ideal gradually mutates into totalitarian tyranny, with a clear and oppressive narrative turn.
Morgurax and the War of the Black Tower give the late game a genuine final examination.
Magic, industry, development, and conquest form a strong feedback loop.
warnings: The War of the Black Tower applies internal unrest and external coalition pressure at the same time.
Diplomatic options are limited; overextending your finances and manpower early is punished in the endgame.
The route includes institutionalised slaughter, corpse enslavement, and exploitation of souls.
Forming Z99 replaces the mission tree and begins a separate campaign.

positive_indicators: The early public goal of improving the lives of the living.
values.rationale: The early ideal of 'the dead labour so the living may prosper' has a public-benefit aspect. The main route, however, institutionalises killing orcs and goblins for labour, the Death Tax, use of souls, purges, and terror rule, making the trajectory clearly radicalising.
red_flags: Killing sapient peoples and converting them into labour.
The Death Tax and exploitation of souls.
